approach:
Add one reading check, `check_part_coverage(reading, request)`, as one new `step!(check_part_coverage(reading, request));` line, last in `refusing_check` (checks.rs:518). A new parser `request_parts` in topics.rs reads numbered parts `(N)`, `N.`, `N)` (runs 1,2,3.. of at least two) and the dash or star bullets of an Acceptance section (all bullets when no opener exists). `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` stay untouched. Quoted or backticked spans, fenced blocks, `>` lines, generated lines and everything after `## Source` are never markers. Guard: `reading.capability.is_none() || reading.question.is_some()` returns Ok (checks.rs:415).

COVERAGE (an item is covered by one of three routes). (i) MARKER CITATION, tightened for finding 7: a criterion covers part N outright only when the marker (`(N)`, `part N`, `item N`) STARTS the criterion after trimming and bullet punctuation. A marker later in the criterion counts only when it stands as its own token (the char before it is start, whitespace or `[`, never an identifier char or `)`), is not part of a range (`(1)-(3)`, `(1)–(3)`, `(1) to (3)`, `parts 1-3`), and the criterion also shares at least one own stem with the item. So `Some(3)` and `(1)-(3)` never cover. A criterion that itself has a deferral phrase never covers. (ii) REGRESSION BULLET: an item with a test-pass phrase whose other own stems all lie in REGRESSION_STEMS {unrel, behav, other, regre, break} is covered by any criterion with a test-pass phrase or `cargo test` (the Steward bullet 'No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass', steward.rs:621-623). 'fmt, clippy and test pass' has the stem `clipp`, so `cargo test` alone does not cover it. (iii) STEM FALLBACK: the item's own distinctive stems (sibling-shared stems removed; all stems when none remain; tokens containing `/` dropped on the item side) must share min(2, ceil(n/2)) stems with one criterion. Items with no stem are unchecked. Reading text is tokenised whole with quoted spans kept.

DEFERRAL (finding 4 fixed). It is searched in summary, assumptions, departures and out_of_scope, never in criteria. Clauses are cut on `;` and on a comma only before a marker or part word. A clause defers an item when it has a deferral phrase (follow-up, deferred, later job, separate job, not in this job, left for), no negation guard (never, without, refus, unless, do not, not defer) and names the item in one of two strengths. STRONG naming: the item's marker, or (for an item with at least 2 own stems) a clause that restates ALL of the item's own stems. A strong deferral refuses the item even when a criterion covers it. WEAK naming is any other overlap of own stems; a weak deferral never refuses a covered item (it only supplies the word 'deferred' in the message for an item that is already uncovered). So '(2) show the timeout in athena status' stays accepted when a criterion covers it and the summary says 'colouring the status output is left for a follow-up job' (shares only `statu`), while 'Part (2) is left for a follow-up job' still refuses. Past guard: a clause is skipped only when a past word (was, were, had been, been, already, previously) sits within the 3 words before the deferral phrase, or the clause has `(earlier|previous|prior|last) (reading|attempt|job|result|run|plan)`, or it names a job id. An out_of_scope item counts only with a deferral phrase naming it strongly, or when it is the whole part (bare marker, or it restates the part's stems and adds none).

SPLIT EXEMPTION per clause (cut on `;` and `,`): modal, no negation, no complaint word, and Shape A (move verb, at most 4 object words with no path-like token, a split-signal adjective before job/change/PR/request, or a plural noun with several/multiple) or Shape B (marker or part word as subject of be/become, then follow-up/separate/later/another job/change/PR). A clause naming markers exempts only those parts; one naming none exempts every item.

FIXTURES. (a) fake.rs `reader_turn` adds one content criterion per request bullet or numbered line, so nested fake runs pass. Finding 6: a numbered part is emitted as `(N): <words>` (marker first, which covers it outright), every copied item is reduced to its plain words (every whitespace word containing `/` or a backtick or quote removed; cap 300 chars), so check_reading_references (checks.rs:408-473, which only reads slash path tokens whose first segment is a top-level directory), the boundary scan and check_criteria_evidence see no path. The fake producer and verifier build their criteria and verdict from the brief's criteria list (fake.rs:328-338, 389-395), so they stay index-matched. (b) CLI tests: `Scenario::default()` has two criteria and `passing_verdict(2)` (common/mod.rs:500; verify.rs:533-543 matches by index), so common/mod.rs is NOT edited. The producer changes request text only: job_plan.rs:166/169 bullets, the drain.rs `complete_request` bullet (committed, no longer conditional, finding 5), and gives tests/proposals.rs its own reading covering the four `accept_request` bullets (finding 3). Never loosen the check.

The reader brief gets no rule; briefs.rs is listed but unchanged. The refusal message carries the repair.

Answers to the quoted findings: (1)(2) job_plan.rs and drain.rs are test fixtures outside the deliverable list, but criterion 8 (`cargo test` passes) cannot hold without them: the new gate refuses their request bullets against the fixed Scenario reading. Only request strings change; no production code, governance file or common/mod.rs. Declared in files and one User question. (3) tests/proposals.rs `accepting_submits_a_job_that_lists_defaults_toml_and_edits_nothing` (proposals.rs:209-242) reaches `accept_proposal` (core proposals.rs:638-642) and `accept_request` (proposals.rs:442-450) writes four dash bullets with no Acceptance opener; the default reading's criteria (README.md greeting, tests pass) cover none, so the test would fail at unwrap. Fix: that test gets its own `scenario.reading` with deliverable defaults.toml (modify) and four criteria covering the bullets; no verdict (the job is only Proposed). The proposal source text (`source_text`, proposals.rs:79-86) holds no records/ path, so a criterion citing it trips nothing in check_reading_references. A corpus Accept case uses the real `accept_request` text; the changelog says defaults-proposal readings must now cover each bullet. (4) strong and weak deferral, above; corpus Accept `covered-part-extension-deferred-shares-stems` and Refuse twin `covered-part-deferred-by-marker`. (5) `complete_request` (drain.rs:6319-6321) bullet becomes `README.md ends with a greeting line`, committed; tests named in dependents. (6) fake copy reduced to plain words with markers cited; three generator-shaped end-to-end cases; risk lists every check a copy can trip. (7) tightened citation above, pinned by `marker_refs` unit tests for 'Some(3)', '(1)-(3)', '(1) to (3)', 'parts 1-3'.

decisions.choice: Distinctive stem order is fixed and written in a code comment: lowercase token; drop trailing s if longer than 4; reject under 4 chars; reject if the raw or singular word is in the stop list (checked BEFORE the cut); cut to 5. Stop list holds domain words (test, tests, pass, passes, change, changes, described, existing, job, part, request, fmt, made, make) and English function words of 4+ letters (with, that, from, each, when, into, only, this, then, than, they, them, have, will, would, should, which, there, their, these, those, also, such, some, same, more, most, must, does, been, being, both, over, under, once, after, before, about, other, used, uses, using, need, needs, where, what). REGRESSION_STEMS is a second const. A unit test pins with/that/from/changes/described/existing/tests/pass as not distinctive, clippy and cover distinctive, default = defaults.
